newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's exports to grow 7 pct in '97,'98 - Kandir.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's exports to grow 7 pct in '97,'98 - Kandir.

text.p: Brazilian exports are likely to grow seven percent a year in 1997 and 1998, said Planning Minister Antonio Kandir.
Kandir said exports are expected to grow 14 percent a year in 1999 and 2000. He said exports should grow in response to recent export-boosting measures including tax exemptions and financing tools.
He added the government is studying new credit lines for exporters at lower interest rates.
The Planning Minister said he expects exports to reach $70 billion in the year 2000. Last year, Brazil exported $47.7 billion.
Speaking at a seminar on private savings, Kandir said Brazil's sustained economic growth depends on an increase in domestic savings.
To raise domestic savings, the government has to focus on privatizations and the pension reform, he said.
Kandir said the Brazilian government plans to sell $25 billion in state assets in the period 1997-1998, of which $10 billion will be this year.

He said $10 billion of that two-year total will be raised in the power sector, $7 billion in telecommunications and the remainder in the sale of state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce and other assets.
With an increase in savings, Kandir expects Brazil's economy to grow six percent a year on average over the next 10 years.
In the year 2006, Brazil's gross domestic product will top $1.3 trillion. Currently, the country's GDP approaches $700 billion.
